flawed_step: The inference that an already-sorted array is a cheap case because it requires no swaps is unjustified: running time is defined by key comparisons, not swaps. With the first element as pivot, each pivot is the smallest key, producing maximally unbalanced subproblems.
counterexample: For every n>=2, take A_n=[1,2,...,n]. The first pivot 1 is compared with the other n-1 keys and leaves a recursive subarray [2,...,n] of size n-1. This repeats, so the comparison count is (n-1)+(n-2)+...+1=n(n-1)/2. For example, [1,2,3,4] gives subproblem sizes 4->3->2->1 and 3+2+1=6 comparisons. Since [n(n-1)/2]/[n log n]=(n-1)/(2 log n) is unbounded, this family is not O(n log n).
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Deterministically choosing the first element makes every ascending sorted array a worst-case input, with quadratic rather than O(n log n) comparison count.
